title.zh: 第二十 郡國二 豫州 冀州
title.en: Volume 110: Commanderies and States Part Two
title.raw: 第二十 郡國二 豫州 冀州 Volume 110: Commanderies and States Part Two

translations.literal: Treatise Twenty: Commanderies and States, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 20: Commanderies and Principalities, Part II

sentences.zh: 颍川 汝南 梁国 沛国 陈国 鲁国

translations.literal: Yingchuan, Runan, the Liang princedom, the Pei princedom, the Chen princedom, the Lu princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Yü Province group: Yingchuan, Runan, Liang, Pei, Chen, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 魏郡 钜鹿 常山 中山 安平 河閒 清河 赵国 勃海

translations.literal: Weijun, Julu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Anping, Hejian, Qinghe, the Zhao princedom, Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province group: Weijun, Julu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Anping, Hejian, Qinghe, Zhao, and Bohai.

translations.literal: Yingchuan Commandery was established under Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan Commandery dates to the Qin foundation.

translations.literal: Five hundred li southeast of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It lies five hundred li southeast of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十七城，户二十六万三千四百四十，口百四十三万六千五百一十三。

translations.idiomatic: Jun Terrace—site of the Xia audience—stood here.
Yongshi city lies within the county.
〖Xiangcheng〗 The Western Bulang stronghold is here.
Yuchi Mountain rises in the county.
〖Kunyang〗 The Zhan River flows through the county.
〖Dingling〗 The Eastern Bulang site lies here.

sentences.zh: 〖颍阴〗有狐宗乡，或曰古狐人亭。

translations.literal: 〖Yinyin〗 There is Huzong township; some say the ancient Huren pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yinyin〗 Huzong settlement—identified with the old Huren outpost.

translations.literal: 〖Yanling〗 In Spring and Autumn times it was called Yan (with the place-name radical).
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yanling〗 Spring and Autumn sources use the form with the place-name radical for ‘Yan.’

translations.literal: There is Shu city; there is Shu ford.
translations.idiomatic: Shu city and the Shu crossing are both noted.

translations.literal: 〖Yangcheng〗 There is Mount Song; Wei water and Ying water rise.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yangcheng〗 Sacred Mount Song; the Wei and Ying rivers have their sources here.
〖Fucheng〗 Ying township—linked to the Ying polity—lies here.

translations.literal: 〖Lunshi〗 Established in the fourth year of Jianchu.
Runan Commandery was established by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Runan Commandery was founded under Emperor Gaozu.

translations.literal: Six hundred fifty li southeast of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred fifty li southeast of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 三十七城，户四十万四千四百四十八，口二百一十万七百八十八。

translations.literal: 〖Pingyu〗 There is Shen pavilion; a former state; Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Pingyu〗 Shen pavilion preserves the old Shen polity of the Ji lineage.
〖Xiping〗 Iron workings lie within the county.

translations.literal: There is Bai pavilion; the former Bai state.
translations.idiomatic: Bai pavilion marks the ground of the Bai polity.

translations.literal: 〖Qisi〗 There is Jiang township; the former Jiang state.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Qisi〗 Jiang township preserves the Jiang polity.

translations.literal: 〖Yang'an〗 There is Dao pavilion; a former state.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yang'an〗 Dao pavilion—the old Dao seat—is noted.
〖Wufang〗 Tangxi pavilion marks the famous sword-forge ground.

translations.literal: There is Jiang pavilion; a former state; Ying surname.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang pavilion preserves the Ying-line Jiang polity.
〖Fubo〗 Marquisate restored during the Yongyuan era.

translations.literal: There is Huang pavilion; the former Huang state; Ying surname.
translations.idiomatic: Huang pavilion marks the Huang polity of the Ying lineage.

sentences.zh: 〖宋〗公国，周名郪丘，汉改为新郪，章帝建初四年徙宋公于此。

translations.literal: 〖Song〗 A ducal state; in Zhou times called Ningqiu; Han changed it to Xinning; in the fourth year of Emperor Zhang's Jianchu the Duke of Song was moved here.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Song〗 Ducal fief: Zhou maps label it Ningqiu; Han rechristened it Xinning; Emperor Zhang's Jianchu 4 transferred the Song duke to this seat.

translations.literal: There is Lai pavilion; a former state.
translations.idiomatic: Lai pavilion preserves an ancient polity.

translations.literal: Formerly Qin (sleep); Guangwu's restoration renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: Once called Qin—the ‘sleep’ toponym—until Guangwu rechristened it at the restoration.
Qin Mound preserves the old name.

translations.literal: 〖Shansang〗 A marquisate; formerly belonged to Pei.
〖Chengfu〗 Formerly belonged to Pei; in Spring and Autumn times called Yi.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Chengfu〗 Listed under Pei; Spring and Autumn texts call it Yi.
Zhanghua Terrace—the Chu viewing stage—stood here.

sentences.zh: 九城，户八万三千三百，口四十三万一千二百八十三。

translations.literal: 〖Suiyang〗 Originally the mound of Yanbo of Song.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Suiyang〗 Ground sacred to Yanbo of Song.

translations.literal: 〖Yu〗 There is Kongtong ground; there is Tong ground; there is Tong pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yu〗 Kongtong tract, Tong tract, and Tong pavilion are all recorded.

translations.literal: There is Lun city; the town of Shaokang.

translations.idiomatic: 〖Dangshan〗 Source of figured stone for inscriptions.

translations.literal: There is Ge township; the former state of Ge Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Ge township preserves the ancient domain of Ge Bo.

translations.literal: 〖Bo〗 Formerly belonged to Shanyang; where Tang set his capital.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Bo〗 Once under Shanyang—capital chosen by King Tang.

translations.literal: The Pei princedom was Qin's Sishui Commandery; Emperor Gaozu changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei princedom: Qin's Sishui circuit, rechristened under Emperor Gaozu.

translations.literal: One thousand two hundred li southeast of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand two hundred li southeast of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 二十一城，户二十万四百九十五，口二十五万一千三百九十三。

translations.idiomatic: 〖Xiao〗 Ancient seat of its own polity.
〖Pei〗 Sishui pavilion—where Liu Bang began his career—lies here.

sentences.zh: 〖丰〗西有大泽，高祖斩白蛇于此。

translations.literal: 〖Feng〗 To the west is a great marsh; Gaozu slew the white serpent here.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Feng〗 Westward stretches the great marsh where Gaozu cut down the white serpent.
The deed occurred at Fenyu pavilion.
〖Zan〗 A settlement whose name is corrupted in the edition survives here.
〖Jiao〗 Gaixia settlement—the field where Xiang Yu fell—lies here.

translations.literal: 〖Qi〗 There is Daze township; Chen She rose here.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Qi〗 Daze township, starting point of Chen She's rebellion.

translations.literal: 〖Lin Sui〗 Formerly Mang; Guangwu renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Lin Sui〗 Once called Mang until Guangwu rechristened it.
〖Zhuyi〗 Marquisate built on the old Zhu seat.
〖Xiang〗 Ancient polity in its own right.

translations.literal: 〖Zhuqiu〗 Formerly belonged to the Liang princedom; there is Chan yuan settlement.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Zhuqiu〗 Transferred from Liang; includes Chan yuan settlement.

sentences.zh: 陈国高帝置为淮阳，章和二年改。

translations.literal: The Chen princedom was set up as Huaiyang by Emperor Gaozu; changed in the second year of Zhanghe.
translations.idiomatic: Chen princedom: founded as Huaiyang under Gaozu, renamed in Emperor Zhang's Zhanghe 2.

translations.literal: Seven hundred li southeast of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred li southeast of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九城，户十一万二千六百五十三，口百五十四万七千五百七十二。

translations.literal: 〖Ku〗 In Spring and Autumn times it was called Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Ku〗 Spring and Autumn texts label it Xiang.

translations.literal: The Lu princedom was Qin's Xue Commandery; Empress Gao changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu princedom: Qin's Xue circuit until Empress Gao reorganized it.

sentences.zh: 本属徐州，光武改属豫州。

translations.literal: Originally belonged to Xuzhou; Guangwu reassigned it to Yüzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han listed it with Xuzhou; Guangwu shifted it to Yüzhou.

sentences.zh: 六城，户七万八千四百四十七，口四十一万一千五百九十。

translations.literal: There is the Granary of the Great Ting clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Ting granaries stood here.

translations.literal: There is Que neighborhood; where Confucius dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Que Lane preserves Confucius's home quarter.
The Wufu crossroads—the junction east of the walls—is noted.

translations.literal: 〖Xue〗 The native state; in Warring States times called Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xue〗 Ancient capital later labeled Xuzhou in Warring States rhetoric.
〖Bian〗 The infamous Robber Spring flows here.

sentences.zh: 右豫州刺史部，郡、国六，县、邑公、侯国九十九。

translations.literal: Right: the Inspectorate of Yü Province — six commanderies and princedoms; ninety-nine counties, towns, ducal seats, and marquisates in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yü Province closes with six jurisdictions and ninety-nine county-level seats.

translations.literal: Weijun Commandery was established by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Weijun Commandery was founded under Emperor Gaozu.

translations.literal: Seven hundred li northeast of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred li northeast of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十五城，户十二万九千三百一十，口六十九万五千六百六。

translations.literal: 〖Ye〗 There is the old Great River channel.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Ye〗 The abandoned Yellow River bed passes here.

translations.literal: There is Fu water; there is Yu city.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu River flows past Yu city—names partly rendered with water radicals in the manuscript.
Jiuhou city—the ruined Shang ward—is noted.
Jiyang settlement—the name partly garbled in the edition—is recorded.
Huang Marsh lies within the county.

translations.literal: 〖Yuancheng〗 Five Deer mound; formerly Shalu; there is Sha pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yuancheng〗 Five Deer wasteland—old Shalu—with Sha pavilion.
〖Wu'an〗 Iron deposits lie within the county.

translations.literal: 〖Quliang〗 A marquisate; formerly belonged to Guangping.
Julu Commandery was established under Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Julu Commandery dates to the Qin foundation.

sentences.zh: 建武十三年省广平国，以其县属。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jianwu the Guangping princedom was abolished and its counties attached.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 13 annexed the dissolved Guangping princedom.

translations.literal: One thousand one hundred li north of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand one hundred li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十五城，户十万九千五百一十七，口六十万二千九十六。

translations.literal: 〖Julu〗 Formerly Great Deer; there is Dalu marsh.
〖Xiaquyang〗 There is Gu settlement; the former Zhai Guzi state.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xiaquyang〗 Gu settlement preserves Zhai Guzi's polity.

translations.literal: The Changshan princedom was established by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Changshan princedom was founded under Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 建武十三年省真定国，以其县属。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jianwu the Zhending princedom was abolished and its counties attached.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 13 dissolved Zhending and merged its counties here.

sentences.zh: 十三城，户九万七千五百，口六十三万一千一百八十四。

translations.literal: 〖Gaoyi〗 Formerly Ye (name damaged in edition); Guangwu renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Gaoyi〗 Earlier transcription corrupted in the text; Guangwu rechristened the seat.

sentences.zh: 有千秋亭、五成陌，光武即位于上此矣。

translations.literal: There are Qianqiu pavilion and Wucheng mo; Guangwu assumed the imperial throne here.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqiu pavilion and the Wucheng divide—where Guangwu took the throne—lie here.
〖Nanxingtang〗 Shijiu Gorge lies within the county.
〖Fangzi〗 Mount Zanhuang; source of the Ji River.

translations.literal: The Zhongshan princedom was established by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan princedom was founded under Emperor Gaozu.

translations.literal: One thousand four hundred li north of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand four hundred li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十三城，户九万七千四百一十二，口六十五万八千一百九十五。

translations.idiomatic: 〖Beiping〗 Iron deposits lie within the county.

translations.literal: 〖Xinshi〗 There is Xianyu pavilion; a former state; Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xinshi〗 Xianyu pavilion marks the old Xianyu polity of the Zi lineage.

translations.literal: 〖Tang〗 There is Zhongren pavilion; there is Zuoren township.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Tang〗 Zhongren pavilion and Zuoren township are recorded.

translations.literal: 〖Anxi〗 Originally Anxian; Emperor Zhang renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Anxi〗 Once Anxian until Emperor Zhang rechristened it.

translations.literal: 〖Hanchang〗 Originally Kujing; Emperor Zhang renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Hanchang〗 Formerly Kujing until Emperor Zhang rechristened it.

translations.literal: 〖Liwu〗 A marquisate; formerly belonged to Zhuo.
Heng Mountain is in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Heng rises to the northwest.

translations.literal: 〖Puyin〗 Originally Quni; Emperor Zhang renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Puyin〗 Once Quni until Emperor Zhang rechristened it.

translations.literal: The Anping princedom was formerly Xindu; established by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Anping princedom: Western Han's Xindu circuit, founded under Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 明帝名乐成，延光元年改。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's taboo touched the name Lecheng; in the first year of Yanguang it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: To honor naming taboos for Emperor Ming, the Lecheng label was revised in Yanguang 1.

translations.literal: Two thousand li north of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十三城，户九万一千四百四十，口六十五万五千一百一十八。

translations.literal: 〖Xindu〗 There are Jiang water and the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xindu〗 The Jiang stream and the Hutuo River flow here.

sentences.zh: 〖观津〗经西有漳水，津名薄落津。

translations.literal: 〖Guanjin〗 West of the highway is Zhang water; the ford is called Boluo Ford.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Guanjin〗 Zhang River lies west of the road; the crossing is Boluo Ford.

translations.literal: 〖Raoyang〗 Originally called Rao; belonged to Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Raoyang〗 Shortened from ancient Rao and administered from Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 河间国文帝置，世祖省属信都，和帝永元二年复故。

translations.literal: The Hejian princedom was established by Emperor Wen; Emperor Guangwu attached it to Xindu; Emperor He's Yongyuan 2 restored the old arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian princedom: founded under Emperor Wen, briefly folded into Xindu under Guangwu, restored in Yongyuan 2.

translations.literal: Two thousand five hundred li north of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand five hundred li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十一城，户九万三千七百五十四，口六十三万四千四百二十一。

translations.idiomatic: Ge city lies within the county.

translations.literal: The Qinghe princedom was established by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe princedom was founded under Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 桓帝建和二年改为甘陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan's Jianhe 2 changed it to Ganling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan rechristened it Ganling in Jianhe 2.

translations.literal: One thousand two hundred eighty li north of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand two hundred eighty li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 七城，户十二万三千九百六十四，口七十六万四百一十八。

translations.literal: 〖Ganling〗 Formerly Cuo; Emperor An renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Ganling〗 Once Cuo until Emperor An rechristened it.
〖Ling〗 Gazetted in the summer of Yongyuan 9.

sentences.zh: 赵国秦邯郸郡，高帝改名。

translations.literal: The Zhao princedom was Qin's Handan Commandery; Emperor Gaozu changed the name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao princedom: Qin's Handan circuit, reorganized under Emperor Gaozu.

translations.literal: One thousand one hundred li north of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand one hundred li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 五城，户三万二千七百一十九，口十八万八千三百八十一。

translations.idiomatic: 〖Handan〗 The layered Cong Terrace overlooks the city.

sentences.zh: 〖襄国〗本邢国，秦为信都，项羽更名。

translations.literal: 〖Xiangguo〗 Originally the Xing state; Qin made it Xindu; Xiang Yu renamed it.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Xiangguo〗 Ancient Xing; Qin recorded it as Xindu until Xiang Yu rechristened it.
Tan Terrace marks the old Jin audience hall.

translations.literal: Bohai Commandery was established by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai Commandery was founded under Emperor Gaozu.

translations.literal: One thousand six hundred li north of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand six hundred li north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 八城，户十三万二千三百八十九，口百一十万六千五百

translations.literal: 〖Yangxin〗 Restored in the first year of Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: 〖Yangxin〗 Seat revived under Emperor An's Yanguang 1.

sentences.zh: 右冀州刺史部，郡、国九，县、邑、侯国百

translations.literal: Right: the Inspectorate of Ji Province — nine commanderies and principalities; one hundred (text breaks off) counties, towns, and marquisates.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji Province section ends with a summary of nine commanderies and principalities and a count of one hundred county-level units, but the line is cut short in the received text after the numeral for one hundred.
